questions.question: A trader allows a discount of 20% on the marked price of the goods. He still manages to make a profit of 20% on the cost price. What will be profit percentage had the trader sold the goods at 12.5% discount ?
questions.questionHtml: A trader allows a discount of 20% on the marked price of the goods. He still manages to make a profit of 20% on the cost price. What will be profit percentage had the trader sold the goods at 12.5% discount ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of CP : MP = (100 − 20) : (100 + 20) = 80 : 120 = 2 : 3.

Let CP = 200 and MP = 300.

New Selling Price at 12.5% discount = 300 − (12.5% of 300) = 262.5.

New Profit = 262.5 − 200 = 62.5.

Profit percentage = (62.5 ÷ 200) × 100 = 31.25%.

∴ The correct answer is 31.25%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Discount = 20%, Profit = 20%, New Discount = 12.5%.

Formula Used:

Relationship between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP): CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%)

⇒ CP / MP = (100 − 20) / (100 + 20) = 80 / 120 = 2 / 3

⇒ Let CP = 200 and MP = 300.

⇒ New Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − 12.5) ÷ 100

⇒ New SP = 300 × 87.5 ÷ 100 = 262.5

⇒ Profit amount = New SP − CP = 262.5 − 200 = 62.5

⇒ Profit % = (Profit amount ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (62.5 ÷ 200) × 100 = 31.25%

∴ The correct answer is 31.25%.

Additional Information

CP and MP Relationship

The direct ratio between Cost Price and Marked Price is given by CP/MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%).

Mark-up Percentage

The percentage by which the cost price is increased to set the marked price: Mark-up % = (MP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts x% and y% are given successively, the effective discount is (x + y − xy/100)%.

questions.question: A trader sells wheat at 20% profit and uses 20% less than the actual measure. His gain % is?
questions.questionHtml: A trader sells wheat at 20% profit and uses 20% less than the actual measure. His gain % is?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the direct formula for total gain percentage in dishonest dealing:

Net Gain % = [ {(100 + %Profit) ÷ (100 − %Less Weight)} − 1 ] × 100

⇒ Net Gain % = [ {(100 + 20) ÷ (100 − 20)} − 1 ] × 100

⇒ Net Gain % = [ {120 ÷ 80} − 1 ] × 100 = [ 1.5 − 1 ] × 100 = 50%

∴ The correct answer is 50%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Claimed Profit Percentage = 20%

Weight Reduction = 20%

Let the Cost Price (CP) of 1000 g of wheat be ₹1000.

⇒ Cost Price (CP) of the weight actually sold (800 g) = ₹800

⇒ Selling Price (SP) charged by the trader = CP of 1000 g + 20% of CP = 1000 + 200 = ₹1200

⇒ Total Profit = SP − Actual CP = 1200 − 800 = ₹400

⇒ Gain Percentage = (Total Profit ÷ Actual CP) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (400 ÷ 800) × 100

⇒ Gain % = 1/2 × 100 = 50%

∴ The correct answer is 50%.

Additional Information

Dishonest Dealer Concept

A dealer makes a profit by either marking up the Cost Price or using false weights. If both are done, the net profit is calculated on the actual cost of the goods delivered.

Profit with False Weight Only

If a dealer sells at cost price but uses a weight of w instead of W, then Gain % = [(W − w) ÷ w] × 100.

Successive Profit Formula

Net Profit % = [{(100 + P1) × (100 + P2) ÷ 1002} − 1] × 100, where P1 is price profit and P2 is weight-based profit.

questions.question: Aarav and Durga together can do a piece of work in 33 days. They worked together for 15 days and then Aarav left the work and Durga alone finished the remaining work in 30 days. Find the number of days in which Aarav alone can do the total work.
questions.questionHtml: Aarav and Durga together can do a piece of work in 33 days. They worked together for 15 days and then Aarav left the work and Durga alone finished the remaining work in 30 days. Find the number of days in which Aarav alone can do the total work.
questions.solution:
Let the efficiency of Aarav be A and the efficiency of Durga be D. According to question, ⇒ (A + D) × 33 = (A + D) × 15 + D × 30 ⇒ 33A + 33D = 15A + 15D + 30D

⇒ 18A = 12D ⇒ A : D = 2 : 3

Days taken by Aarav to complete the work = 165/2 days.

questions.question: If Sarita had walked at a speed of 15 km/h instead of 10 km/h, she would have walked 40 km more in the same time. What is the actual distance travelled by her?
questions.questionHtml: If Sarita had walked at a speed of 15 km/h instead of 10 km/h, she would have walked 40 km more in the same time. What is the actual distance travelled by her?
questions.solution:
Distance = Speed × Time

Let the time be T.

⇒ 15T – 10T = 40 ⇒ 5T = 40 ⇒ T = 8 hours

Actual distance covered = (10 × 8) = 80 km

questions.question: The curved surface area (in cm²) of a right circular cone is 2145 π and the radius of its base is 33 cm. What is its volume (in cm³ )?
questions.questionHtml: The curved surface area (in cm²) of a right circular cone is 2145π and the radius of its base is 33 cm. What is its volume (in cm³ )?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Slant height (l) = Curved Surface Area ÷ (π × r) = 2145π ÷ (33π) = 65 cm.

Vertical height (h) = √(l2 − r2) = √(652 − 332) = 56 cm.

Volume = (1/3) × π × r2 × h = (1/3) × π × 33 × 33 × 56.

Volume = 11 × 33 × 56 × π = 20328π cm3.

∴ The correct answer is 20328 π cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of the cone = 2145π cm2

Radius (r) of the base = 33 cm

Formula Used:

1. CSA = π × r × l (where l is the slant height)

2. l2 = r2 + h2 (where h is the vertical height)

3. Volume (V) = (1/3) × π × r2 × h

Calculations:

⇒ 2145π = π × 33 × l

⇒ l = 2145 ÷ 33

⇒ l = 65 cm

⇒ h2 = l2 − r2

⇒ h2 = 652 − 332

⇒ h2 = (65 + 33)(65 − 33) = 98 × 32

⇒ h = √(3136) = 56 cm

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × π × 33 × 33 × 56

⇒ Volume = π × 11 × 33 × 56

⇒ Volume = 20328π cm3

∴ The correct answer is 20328 π cm3.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cone

The TSA includes both the curved surface area and the base area: TSA = πrl + πr2 = πr(l + r).

Relationship with Cylinder

For the same radius and height, the volume of a cone is exactly 1/3rd the volume of a cylinder: Vcone = (1/3)Vcylinder.

Slant Height and Pythagoras

The radius, vertical height, and slant height of a right circular cone always form a right-angled triangle: l = √(h2 + r2).

questions.question: Two circles having equal radius intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of the other. Length of the common chord is 24 cm , then what will be the diameter of each circle?
questions.questionHtml: Two circles having equal radius intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of the other. Length of the common chord is 24 cm, then what will be the diameter of each circle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two equal circles passing through each other's centers, the common chord length is given by: L = √3 × r.

⇒ 24 = √3 × r

⇒ r = 24 / √3 = 8√3 cm

⇒ Diameter of the circle (d) = 2 × r = 2 × 8√3

⇒ d = 16√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 16√3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of both circles = r cm

Length of the common chord (AB) = 24 cm

Formula Used:

In a triangle, the line joining the centers of two circles is the perpendicular bisector of their common chord. Pythagoras theorem: Hypotenuse2 = Base2 + Perpendicular2.

Calculations:

Let O1 and O2 be the centers of the two circles.

⇒ O1O2 = Radius (r) (since each passes through the other's center)

⇒ In ΔO1MA, where M is the midpoint of AB and O1O2:

⇒ AM = AB ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm

⇒ O1M = O1O2 ÷ 2 = r ÷ 2

⇒ O1A = Radius = r

⇒ Using Pythagoras theorem: O1A2 = O1M2 + AM2

⇒ r2 = (r/2)2 + 122

⇒ r2 − r2/4 = 144

⇒ 3r2 / 4 = 144

⇒ r2 = (144 × 4) ÷ 3 = 48 × 4 = 192

⇒ r = √192 = 8√3 cm

⇒ Diameter = 2 × r = 2 × 8√3 = 16√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 16√3 cm.

Additional Information

Common Chord Property

The line joining the centers of two intersecting circles is the perpendicular bisector of their common chord.

Intersecting Equal Circles

When two equal circles pass through each other's centers, they form two equilateral triangles with the intersection points and the centers, all sides being equal to the radius r.

Common Chord Length Formula

If two circles of radii r1 and r2 have centers at distance d, the length of the common chord is 2 × √[r12 − ((r12 − r22 + d2) ÷ 2d)2].

questions.question: In a triangle PQR, PQ : PR = 5 : 3, QR = 18 cm. QP is produced to T, and the bisector of the Angle RPT meets QR produced at S. What is the length (in cm) of RS?
questions.questionHtml: In a triangle PQR, PQ : PR = 5 : 3, QR = 18 cm. QP is produced to T, and the bisector of the Angle RPT meets QR produced at S. What is the length (in cm) of RS?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

According to the External Angle Bisector Theorem, the external bisector of an angle of a triangle divides the opposite side externally in the ratio of the sides containing the angle.

For triangle PQR, with external bisector PS meeting QR produced at S:

PQ ÷ PR = SQ ÷ SR

Given PQ : PR = 5 : 3 and QR = 18 cm.

Let RS = x, then SQ = 18 + x.

⇒ 5 ÷ 3 = (18 + x) ÷ x

⇒ 5x = 54 + 3x ⇒ 2x = 54 ⇒ x = 27

∴ The correct answer is 27 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of sides PQ : PR = 5 : 3

Length of side QR = 18 cm

PS is the exterior angle bisector of angle P.

Formula Used:

In ▵PQR, if the external bisector of ∠P intersects the extension of QR at S, then:

PQ ÷ PR = (QR + RS) ÷ RS

Calculations:

⇒ Let the length of RS be x cm.

⇒ From the theorem, PQ ÷ PR = (QR + RS) ÷ RS

⇒ 5 ÷ 3 = (18 + x) ÷ x

⇒ 5 × x = 3 × (18 + x)

⇒ 5x = 54 + 3x

⇒ 5x − 3x = 54

⇒ 2x = 54

⇒ x = 54 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 27 cm

∴ The correct answer is 27 cm.

Additional Information

Internal Angle Bisector Theorem

The internal bisector of an angle divides the opposite side in the ratio of the other two sides. Formula: BD ÷ DC = AB ÷ AC.

Angle between Bisectors

The internal and external angle bisectors of the same vertex of a triangle are always perpendicular to each other (angle between them is 90°).

Apollonius' Circle

The set of all points where the ratio of distances from two fixed points is constant forms a circle. The internal and external bisectors mark the diameter endpoints of this circle on the base line.

questions.question: The average of the first five natural numbers is 3. Find a new average after adding 6.
questions.questionHtml: The average of the first five natural numbers is 3. Find a new average after adding 6.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Change in average = (New Value − Old Average) ÷ New Total Count

Change = (6 − 3) ÷ 6 = 3 ÷ 6 = 0.5

New average = 3 + 0.5 = 3.5

∴ The correct answer is 3.5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Average of the first 5 natural numbers = 3

New observation added = 6

Formula Used:

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total count

⇒ Sum of the first 5 natural numbers = 3 × 5 = 15

⇒ New total sum = 15 + 6 = 21

⇒ New total count of numbers = 5 + 1 = 6

⇒ New average = 21 ÷ 6 = 3.5

∴ The correct answer is 3.5.

Additional Information

Average of n natural numbers

The average of the first n natural numbers is calculated using the formula: (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Sum of n natural numbers

The total sum of the first n natural numbers is given by the expression: [n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2.

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For any sequence in Arithmetic Progression, the average is always (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

questions.question: Ted spends 55% of his income. His income increases by 28% and his expenditure also increases by 40%. The percentage of increase in his savings is:
questions.questionHtml: Ted spends 55% of his income. His income increases by 28% and his expenditure also increases by 40%. The percentage of increase in his savings is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Expenditure : Savings = 55 : 45 = 11 : 9

Using weighted average: Total % Increase in Income = (RatioExp × % IncreaseExp + RatioSav × % IncreaseSav) ÷ Total Ratio

28 = (11 × 40 + 9 × S) ÷ 20

560 = 440 + 9S

120 = 9S ⇒ S = 13.33%

∴ The correct answer is 13.3%.

Alternate Method

Given: Expenditure = 55% of Income. Income increase = 28%. Expenditure increase = 40%.

Formula: Income = Expenditure + Savings

Let initial Income = 100

⇒ Old Expenditure = 55

⇒ Old Savings = 100 − 55 = 45

⇒ New Income = 100 + (28% of 100) = 128

⇒ New Expenditure = 55 + (40% of 55) = 55 + 22 = 77

⇒ New Savings = 128 − 77 = 51

⇒ Increase in Savings = 51 − 45 = 6

⇒ Percentage increase in Savings = (6 ÷ 45) × 100

⇒ (2 ÷ 15) × 100 = 13.33%

∴ The correct answer is 13.3%.

Additional Information

Income-Expenditure Rule

Income is the sum of Expenditure and Savings. Any change in Income must equal the sum of the absolute changes in Expenditure and Savings.

Weighted Average Method

Percent change in Income = (E × %ΔE + S × %ΔS) ÷ (E + S), where E and S are Expenditure and Savings amounts or ratios.

Percentage Increase Formula

Percentage change = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

questions.question: Rs. 1, 50 paisa and 25 paisa coins are present in a bag in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. If the total amount in the bag is Rs. 684 then find the number of 50 paisa coins in the bag.
questions.questionHtml: Rs. 1, 50 paisa and 25 paisa coins are present in a bag in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. If the total amount in the bag is Rs. 684 then find the number of 50 paisa coins in the bag.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of values = (₹1 × 2) : (₹0.50 × 3) : (₹0.25 × 5) = 2 : 1.5 : 1.25 = 8 : 6 : 5.

Total units for value = 8 + 6 + 5 = 19 units → ₹684.

1 unit = 684 ÷ 19 = 36.

Number of 50 paisa coins = (Value parts for 50p × 36) ÷ Denomination = (6 × 36) ÷ 0.50 = 216 × 2 = 432.

∴ The correct answer is 432 coins.

Alternate Method

Given: Ratio of ₹1, 50 paisa, and 25 paisa coins = 2 : 3 : 5. Total amount = ₹684.

Formula Used: Total Value = ∑(Number of Coins × Value of each Coin)

⇒ Let the number of coins be 2x, 3x, and 5x.

⇒ Total value = (2x × 1) + (3x × 0.50) + (5x × 0.25) = 684

⇒ 2x + 1.5x + 1.25x = 684

⇒ 4.75x = 684

⇒ x = 684 ÷ 4.75

⇒ x = 144

⇒ Number of 50 paisa coins = 3x = 3 × 144 = 432

∴ The correct answer is 432 coins.

Additional Information

Denomination Relationship

The value of a collection of coins is found by Number of Coins × Face Value. Ensure all face values are in the same currency unit (e.g., all in ₹ or all in Paise).

Ratio of Values vs Ratio of Counts

If the number of coins is in ratio a:b:c and denominations are d1, d2, d3, then the ratio of their total values is (a×d1) : (b×d2) : (c×d3).

Inverse Proportion Case

When the total values of different denominations are equal, the number of coins is inversely proportional to the face value of the coins.

questions.question: If (6) x+5 ÷ (6) -2x+3 = (6) 2x-5 × [(6) -2 ] x+4 , then what is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: If (6)<sup>x+5</sup> ÷ (6)<sup>-2x+3</sup> = (6)<sup>2x-5</sup> × [(6)<sup>-2</sup>]<sup>x+4</sup>, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Given:

(6)x+5 ÷ (6)-2x+3 = (6)2x-5 × [(6)-2]x+4

Formula used:

am/an = am - n 

am x an = am + n 

(am)n = amn 

Calculation:

⇒ (6)x+5 ÷ (6)-2x+3 = (6)2x-5 × [(6)-2]x+4

⇒ (6)x+5-(-2x+3) = (6)2x-5 × (6)-2(x+4)

⇒ (6)3x + 2 = (6)2x - 5 × 6(- 2x - 8) 

⇒ (6)3x + 2 = (6)(2x - 5 + -2x - 8) 

On comparing the powers of 6 on both sides,

3x + 2 = 2x - 5 + -2x - 8

3x + 2 = -13

3x = -15

x = -15/3 

x = - 5 

∴ The correct answer is -5.

questions.question: If a sum of money doubles in 5 years at simple interest, then what is the rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: If a sum of money doubles in 5 years at simple interest, then what is the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a sum of money doubles in simple interest, the interest earned (SI) is 100% of the principal.

Shortcut formula: Rate % = 100 ÷ Time

Rate % = 100 ÷ 5 = 20%

Convert percentage to decimal: 20 ÷ 100 = 0.2

∴ The correct answer is 0.2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = P

Amount (A) = 2P

Time (T) = 5 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = Amount (A) − Principal (P)

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 2P − P = P

⇒ P = (P × R × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ 1 = (R × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ 5 × R = 100

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 5 = 20%

⇒ Rate in decimal form = 20 ÷ 100 = 0.2

∴ The correct answer is 0.2.

Additional Information

General N-times Formula

If a sum of money becomes n times in T years at simple interest, then Rate (R) = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ T.

Simple Interest definition

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal amount of a loan or deposit, so the interest amount is constant every year.

Percentage to Decimal Conversion

To convert a percentage to a decimal, divide the number by 100. For example, 20% = 20 ÷ 100 = 0.2.

questions.question: If x 2 + y 2 = 106 and x - y = 4, then the value of \(\rm \frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{y}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If x2 + y2 = 106 and x - y = 4, then the value of \(\rm \frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{y}\) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify two numbers x and y such that x − y = 4 and x2 + y2 = 106.

By inspection, if x = 9 and y = 5, then 9 − 5 = 4 and 92 + 52 = 81 + 25 = 106.

The required expression is 1/x − 1/y.

Substituting the values: 1/9 − 1/5 = (5 − 9) / 45 = −4/45.

∴ The correct answer is −4/45.

Alternate Method

Given:

x2 + y2 = 106

x − y = 4

Formula Used:

⇒ Algebraic Identity: (x − y)2 = x2 + y2 − 2xy

⇒ Reciprocal Difference: 1/x − 1/y = (y − x) / xy

Calculations:

⇒ x − y = 4

⇒ Squaring both sides: (x − y)2 = 42

⇒ x2 + y2 − 2xy = 16

⇒ 106 − 2xy = 16

⇒ 2xy = 106 − 16 = 90

⇒ xy = 45

⇒ Required value = 1/x − 1/y = (y − x) / xy

⇒ Since x − y = 4, then y − x = −4

⇒ Value = −4/45

∴ The correct answer is −4/45.

Additional Information

Square of Sum Identity

(x + y)2 = x2 + y2 + 2xy. This is used to find the sum of variables when the sum of squares and product are known.

Relation between Sum and Difference

(x + y)2 − (x − y)2 = 4xy. This identity directly relates the sum, difference, and product of two variables.

Difference of Squares

x2 − y2 = (x − y)(x + y). Useful for factorizing expressions involving squares.

Cubic Identity

x3 − y3 = (x − y)(x2 + xy + y2). Used for higher degree algebraic simplifications.

questions.question: Trains P and Q are running in the same direction on parallel tracks with speeds of x km/h and 90 km/h (90 > x), respectively. The faster train passes a man sitting in the slower train in 30 seconds. If the length of train Q is 225 m, then what is the value of x ?
questions.questionHtml: Trains P and Q are running in the same direction on parallel tracks with speeds of x km/h and 90 km/h (90 > x), respectively. The faster train passes a man sitting in the slower train in 30 seconds. If the length of train Q is 225 m, then what is the value of x ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 225 m ÷ 30 sec = 7.5 m/s.

Convert m/s to km/h: 7.5 × (18/5) = 1.5 × 18 = 27 km/h.

Since trains are in the same direction: SpeedQ − SpeedP = 27 km/h.

90 − x = 27 ⇒ x = 63 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 63.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of Train Q (SQ) = 90 km/h

Speed of Train P (SP) = x km/h

Length of Train Q (LQ) = 225 m

Time taken to pass the man = 30 sec

Formula Used:

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = S1 − S2

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Relative Speed = (90 − x) km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = (90 − x) × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Distance = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ 225 = (90 − x) × (5/18) × 30

⇒ 225 = (90 − x) × (150/18)

⇒ 225 = (90 − x) × (25/3)

⇒ (225 × 3) ÷ 25 = 90 − x

⇒ 9 × 3 = 90 − x

⇒ 27 = 90 − x

⇒ x = 90 − 27

⇒ x = 63

∴ The correct answer is 63.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concepts

When moving in the same direction, relative speed is S1 − S2. In the opposite direction, it is S1 + S2.

Train passing a Man vs Train

If a train passes a man in another train, the distance is only the length of the passing train. If it passes the whole train, the distance is the sum of both lengths.

Speed Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 4 hours, B and C together in 3 hours, and A and C together in 2 hours. How long will B alone take to do it ?
questions.questionHtml: A can do a piece of work in 4 hours, B and C together in 3 hours, and A and C together in 2 hours. How long will B alone take to do it ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Total Work be 12 units (LCM of 4, 3, and 2).

Efficiency of A = 12 ÷ 4 = 3; Efficiency of (B + C) = 12 ÷ 3 = 4; Efficiency of (A + C) = 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

Efficiency of C = Eff(A+C) − Eff(A) = 6 − 3 = 3 units/hr.

Efficiency of B = Eff(B+C) − Eff(C) = 4 − 3 = 1 unit/hr.

Time taken by B alone = 12 ÷ 1 = 12 hr.

∴ The correct answer is 12 hr.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by A = 4 hr

Time taken by B and C together = 3 hr

Time taken by A and C together = 2 hr

Formula Used:

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

Person Days (Time) Total Work Efficiency
A 4 hr 12 units 3
B & C 3 hr 4
A & C 2 hr 6

Calculations:

⇒ Efficiency of A = 3 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of B + C = 4 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of A + C = 6 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + C) − Efficiency of A

⇒ Efficiency of C = 6 − 3 = 3 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of B = Efficiency of (B + C) − Efficiency of C

⇒ Efficiency of B = 4 − 3 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken by B = 12 ÷ 1 = 12 hr

∴ The correct answer is 12 hr.

Additional Information

Relationship between Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the Time taken to complete a work. Efficiency = 1 ÷ Time (when work is constant).

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the ratio of the work done by individuals. If they work for the same amount of time, the wage ratio is equal to their Efficiency ratio.

Combined Efficiency

When multiple people work together, their net efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies. Efficiency(A+B) = EfficiencyA + EfficiencyB.

questions.question: If cot x = \(\frac{4}{3}\) then find the value of \(\frac{sin \ x - cos \ x}{sin \ x + cos \ x}\)
questions.questionHtml: If cot x = \(\frac{4}{3}\) then find the value of \(\frac{sin \ x - cos \ x}{sin \ x + cos \ x}\)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Divide the numerator and denominator of the given expression by sin x.

⇒ (sin x − cos x) ÷ sin x = 1 − cot x

⇒ (sin x + cos x) ÷ sin x = 1 + cot x

⇒ Result = (1 − cot x) / (1 + cot x) = (1 − 4/3) / (1 + 4/3)

⇒ Result = (−1/3) / (7/3) = −1/7

∴ The correct answer is −1/7.

Alternate Method

Given: cot x = 4/3

Formula Used: cot x = Base / Perpendicular | sin x = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse | cos x = Base / Hypotenuse

⇒ In the right-angled triangle ABC, let Base (AB) = 4 and Perpendicular (BC) = 3.

⇒ Hypotenuse (AC) = √(AB2 + BC2) = √(42 + 32) = √(16 + 9) = 5

⇒ sin x = BC/AC = 3/5 and cos x = AB/AC = 4/5

⇒ Target value = (sin x − cos x) / (sin x + cos x)

⇒ Target value = (3/5 − 4/5) / (3/5 + 4/5)

⇒ Target value = (−1/5) / (7/5)

⇒ Target value = −1/7

∴ The correct answer is −1/7.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin2x + cos2x = 1 and 1 + cot2x = cosec2x.

Quotient Relations

The function cot x is defined as the ratio of cos x / sin x or the reciprocal 1 / tan x.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets of integers satisfying a2 + b2 = c2 include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

questions.question: When 10 is subtracted from each of the given observations, the mean is reduced to 60%. If 5 is added to all the given observations, the mean will be:
questions.questionHtml: When 10 is subtracted from each of the given observations, the mean is reduced to 60%. If 5 is added to all the given observations, the mean will be:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

A decrease of 10 in each observation reduces the mean by exactly 10.

Since the mean is reduced to 60%, the reduction of 10 represents 100% − 60% = 40% of the original mean.

40% of Original Mean = 10 ⇒ 100% of Original Mean = (10 ÷ 40) × 100 = 25.

When 5 is added to all observations, the mean also increases by 5.

New Mean = 25 + 5 = 30.

∴ The correct answer is 30.

Alternate Method

Given:

Reduction in each value = 10

New mean percentage = 60% of original

Constant added later = 5

Let the original mean of the observations be M.

According to the property of averages, if a constant is subtracted from every observation, the mean is reduced by that same constant.

⇒ M − 10 = 60% of M

⇒ M − 10 = 0.6M

⇒ M − 0.6M = 10

⇒ 0.4M = 10

⇒ M = 10 ÷ 0.4 = 25

Now, if 5 is added to all given observations, the mean will also increase by 5:

⇒ New Mean = M + 5

⇒ New Mean = 25 + 5

⇒ New Mean = 30

∴ The correct answer is 30.

Additional Information

Effect of Addition/Subtraction on Mean

If a constant k is added to or subtracted from each observation, the mean of the new set of observations is the original mean plus or minus k.

Effect of Multiplication/Division on Mean

If each observation is multiplied or divided by a non-zero constant k, the mean is also multiplied or divided by k.

General Linear Transformation

For any data set x, if yi = axi + b, then the new mean Y = aX + b, where X is the original mean.

questions.questionHtml: 'P' and 'Q' entered into a partnership investing Rs. 30000 and Rs. 35000 respectively. After 4 months, 'R' also joined the business with an investment of Rs. 40000. What is the share of 'R' in the annual profit of Rs. 50000?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Profit Ratio = (Investment × Time)

P : Q : R = (30000 × 12) : (35000 × 12) : (40000 × 8)

P : Q : R = 360000 : 420000 : 320000 = 36 : 42 : 32 = 18 : 21 : 16

Total ratio units = 18 + 21 + 16 = 55 units

Share of R = (16 ÷ 55) × 50000 = 160000 ÷ 11 ≈ 14545.5

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 14545.5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Investment of P = Rs. 30000

Investment of Q = Rs. 35000

Investment of R = Rs. 40000

Time period for P = 12 months (since profit is calculated annually)

Time period for Q = 12 months

Time period for R = 12 − 4 = 8 months (joined after 4 months)

Annual Profit = Rs. 50000

Formula Used:

Profit Share Ratio = (Capital1 × Time1) : (Capital2 × Time2) : (Capital3 × Time3)

Calculations:

⇒ Profit Ratio (P : Q : R) = (30000 × 12) : (35000 × 12) : (40000 × 8)

⇒ Profit Ratio = 360000 : 420000 : 320000

⇒ Profit Ratio = 36 : 42 : 32

⇒ Profit Ratio = 18 : 21 : 16

⇒ Total Ratio Units = 18 + 21 + 16 = 55 units

⇒ 55 units = Rs. 50000

⇒ 1 unit = 50000 ÷ 55 = 10000 ÷ 11

⇒ Share of R = 16 units

⇒ Share of R = 16 × (10000 ÷ 11) = 160000 ÷ 11

⇒ Share of R = 14545.4545...

⇒ Share of R ≈ Rs. 14545.5

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 14545.5.

Additional Information

Simple Partnership

When all partners invest capital for the exact same duration, the profit is distributed purely in the ratio of their respective initial investments.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest capital for different time durations, the final profit ratio is obtained by taking the product of the capital and the time period of investment for each partner.

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner typically receives a fixed active salary or a specific percentage of the total profit for managing the business. The remaining profit is then distributed among all partners (including sleeping partners) based on their capital-time ratios.

Circle Area 154 → Radius (r) = 7 cm (Standard value).

Side of Triangle (a) = 44 ÷ 3 = 14.66 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 93.1 cm2.

Given: Area of Circle = 154 cm2, Shape changed from Circle to Equilateral Triangle.

Formula Used: Area of Circle = πr2; Circumference = 2πr; Area of Equilateral Triangle = (√3/4)a2.

⇒ πr2 = 154

⇒ (22/7) × r2 = 154

⇒ r2 = (154 × 7) ÷ 22 = 49

⇒ Radius (r) = √49 = 7 cm

⇒ Length of wire = 2 × (22/7) × 7 = 44 cm

⇒ Perimeter of Triangle = 3 × Side (a) = 44 cm

⇒ a = 44/3 cm

⇒ Area of Triangle = (√3/4) × (44/3)2

⇒ Area = (√3/4) × (1936/9) = 484√3/9

⇒ Area ≈ (484 × 1.732) ÷ 9 ≈ 93.14 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 93.1 cm2.

Additional Information

Perimeter vs Area Consistency

When a wire of fixed length L is bent into different shapes, the Circle always encloses the maximum area, followed by a square and then an equilateral triangle.

questions.question: A sum of money was put at simple interest at a certain rate for 2 years. If it had been at 1% higher rate, then it would have fetched Rs. 180 more. What is the sum ?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money was put at simple interest at a certain rate for 2 years. If it had been at 1% higher rate, then it would have fetched Rs. 180 more. What is the sum ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The extra interest is generated by the increased rate over the given time.

Effective increase in interest % = 1% × 2 years = 2%

⇒ 2% of Principal = ₹180

⇒ 100% (Principal) = (180 ÷ 2) × 100 = ₹9000

∴ The correct answer is ₹9000.

Alternate Method

Given: Time (T) = 2 years, Rate Increase = 1% per annum, Extra Interest = ₹180.

Formula Used: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Let the original Principal be P and original Rate be R.

⇒ Original SI = (P × R × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ New SI = (P × (R + 1) × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ New SI − Original SI = 180

⇒ [(2P × (R + 1)) ÷ 100] − [2PR ÷ 100] = 180

⇒ (2P ÷ 100) × (R + 1 − R) = 180

⇒ 2P ÷ 100 = 180

⇒ P = (180 × 100) ÷ 2

⇒ P = 90 × 100 = 9000

∴ The correct answer is ₹9000.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Property

Simple interest is directly proportional to the principal, rate, and time. If the rate increases by x% for T years, the total interest increases by (P × x × T) ÷ 100.

Rate vs Interest Change

When the principal and time are constant, the ratio of the change in interest is equal to the ratio of the change in rate: (SI1 − SI2) = P × T × (R1 − R2) ÷ 100.

Principal Formula

If the difference in interest (D) is known for a change in rate (r) over time (T), then Principal (P) = (D × 100) ÷ (r × T).

questions.question: What should be subtracted from x 4 + x 3 - 2x 2 + x + 1 such that it is divisible by x – 1?
questions.questionHtml: What should be subtracted from x<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>3</sup> - 2x<sup>2</sup> + x + 1 such that it is divisible by x – 1?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

To make a polynomial P(x) divisible by (x − a), the remainder P(a) must be subtracted from it.

According to the Remainder Theorem, put x = 1 (from x − 1 = 0) into the expression.

Calculation: 14 + 13 − 2(1)2 + 1 + 1 ⇒ 1 + 1 − 2 + 1 + 1 = 2.

The remainder is 2, so 2 must be subtracted to make the expression divisible.

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Alternate Method

Given: Polynomial P(x) = x4 + x3 − 2x2 + x + 1 and Divisor = (x − 1).

Formula Used: The Remainder Theorem states that when a polynomial P(x) is divided by (x − a), the remainder is P(a).

⇒ Let the value to be subtracted be k.

⇒ For the expression (x4 + x3 − 2x2 + x + 1 − k) to be exactly divisible by (x − 1), the remainder must be 0.

⇒ By Factor Theorem, P(1) − k = 0.

⇒ (1)4 + (1)3 − 2(1)2 + (1) + 1 − k = 0

⇒ 1 + 1 − 2 + 1 + 1 − k = 0

⇒ 2 − k = 0

⇒ k = 2

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Additional Information

Remainder Theorem

It states that if a polynomial P(x) is divided by (x − a), then the remainder is equal to P(a).

Factor Theorem

A polynomial P(x) has a factor (x − a) if and only if P(a) = 0. This is a special case of the remainder theorem.

Division Algorithm for Polynomials

P(x) = g(x) × q(x) + r(x), where g(x) is the divisor, q(x) is the quotient, and r(x) is the remainder.

  • Percentages and fractions can be plural or singular. It depends upon the noun that follows them. If the word that follows the fraction or percentage is singular, you'll use a singular verb. If the word following the fraction is plural, use a plural verb.

  • Sentence (C) is INCORRECT.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Having released on bail , the minister went to meet his colleagues.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

Having released on bail, the minister went to meet his colleagues.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Having been released on bail'.

Key Points

  • Having + past participle expresses the cause and effect of an action in a sentence. The cause of the sentence is expressed first and its effect is expressed later.
  • Both are joined by the subject because generally, the subject has done the action. But, when the subject isn't responsible for the cause or action, it is expressed in a passive voice.
    • Example: Having lost her jewel, she was sad. (Correct)
      • In the above-given example, the effect is 'she was sad' and the cause is that she lost her jewel. This sentence can be written as - She lost her jewel, and she was sad. In both sentences the subject is 'she', thus, it doesn't require the passive use of sentence.
    • ​Example: Having found guilty of theft, Gyan was sentenced to two-year imprisonment. (Incorrect)
      • The above sentence is incorrect. In the above-given sentence, the effect is 'Gyan was sentenced to two-year imprisonment', the cause of this action is that he was found guilty by police. The above sentence can be written as - Police found him guilty, Gyan was sentenced to two-year imprisonment. When the subject of cause and effect is not the same then the cause is written in passive voice. Thus, the correct sentence would be - Having been found guilty, Gyan was sentenced to two-year imprisonment.
  • Thus, the correct answer is option 1.
     

Correct sentence: Having been released on bail, the minister went to meet his colleagues. 

Additional Information

  • Passive voice: a form or set of forms of a verb in which the subject undergoes the action of the verb.

questions.question: Which wire, among three wires of the same material but different lengths (L, 2L, and 3L), will experience the maximum heat losses when the same current is passed through all of them?
questions.questionHtml: Which wire, among three wires of the same material but different lengths (L, 2L, and 3L), will experience the maximum heat losses when the same current is passed through all of them?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.

Key Points

  • The heat produced in a wire due to the passage of electric current is given by the formula:
    • H=I2Rt,
    • Where
      H is the heat produced, I is the current,  R is the resistance, and t is the time.
  • For wires of the same material but different lengths, their resistance is directly proportional to their length (given the same cross-sectional area).
  • Since the wires have the same volume, the wire of length 3L will have the highest resistance, followed by the wire of length 2L, and then the wire of length  L .
  • With the same current passing through all wires, the wire with the highest resistance (i.e., the wire of length 3L ) will experience the maximum heat losses.
  • Therefore, the wire of length 3L will have the maximum heat losses among the three wires.

  • Nimbostratus (2): Clouds with a large vertical extent, often associated with continuous rain or snow.
  • Altostratus (4): Mid-altitude clouds, found between 6,500 and 20,000 feet.
  • Cirrocumulus (1): High-altitude clouds forming a layer.
  • Cirrus (3): High-altitude clouds.

Additional Information
  • Clouds are visible collections of tiny water droplets or ice crystals suspended in the Earth's atmosphere.
  • They form as a result of the condensation of water vapor into liquid or solid particles.
  • Clouds play a crucial role in the Earth's climate system by influencing weather patterns and reflecting sunlight.
  • Types of Clouds Based on Height:
    • High-Level Clouds (Above 20,000 feet):
      • Cirrus (Ci): Wispy, feathery clouds at high altitudes.
      • Cirrostratus (Cs): Thin ice-crystal clouds covering the sky, often creating halos around the sun or moon.
      • Cirrocumulus (Cc): Small, white patches of clouds often arranged in rows.
    • Mid-Level Clouds (6,500 to 20,000 feet):
      • Altostratus (As): Gray or blue-gray clouds covering the sky, often preceding storms with continuous rain or snow.

      • Clouds with Vertical Development:

questions.question: The "Dalit Panthers" movement, inspired by the Black Panthers in the United States, primarily focused on:
questions.questionHtml: The "Dalit Panthers" movement, inspired by the Black Panthers in the United States, primarily focused on:

options.text: Promoting Dalit entrepreneurship and economic empowerment
options.html: Promoting Dalit entrepreneurship and economic empowerment

options.text: Advocating for the inclusion of Dalits in mainstream political parties
options.html: Advocating for the inclusion of Dalits in mainstream political parties

options.html: Challenging caste-based discrimination and asserting Dalit identity

options.text: Encouraging the assimilation of Dalits into the dominant caste culture
options.html: Encouraging the assimilation of Dalits into the dominant caste culture

questions.solution:
Answer: The correct answer is, c) Challenging caste-based discrimination and asserting Dalit identity.

Solution:
The Dalit Panthers movement emerged in the 1970s in Maharashtra, India, as a radical and militant organization inspired by the Black Panthers in the United States. The movement's primary focus was to challenge the deeply entrenched caste-based discrimination faced by Dalits (formerly known as "untouchables") and assert Dalit identity with pride. The Dalit Panthers sought to mobilize the Dalit community to fight against the oppressive caste system, social injustice, and the denial of basic human rights.

 Key Points

  • Militant Activism: The Dalit Panthers adopted a militant and confrontational approach to challenge the caste system and demand justice for Dalits. They organized protests, demonstrations, and rallies to draw attention to the issues faced by the Dalit community and put pressure on the government and society to address these problems.
  • Assertion of Dalit Identity: The movement sought to instill a sense of pride and self-respect among Dalits by rejecting the stigma and shame associated with their caste identity. The Dalit Panthers encouraged Dalits to assert their identity and challenge the dominant caste narratives that perpetuated their oppression.
  • Literary Expression and Cultural Assertion: The Dalit Panthers used literature, poetry, and other forms of artistic expression as powerful tools to articulate the experiences, struggles, and aspirations of the Dalit community. Dalit writers and poets played a significant role in the movement, using their works to challenge caste-based discrimination and assert Dalit identity.
  • Intersectionality and Solidarity: The Dalit Panthers recognized the intersectionality of caste, class, and gender oppression and sought to build solidarity with other marginalized communities facing similar struggles. They forged alliances with progressive movements, left-wing organizations, and feminist groups to create a broader platform for social justice.
  • Demand for Political Representation: The movement advocated for increased political representation of Dalits and challenged the domination of upper-caste individuals in political institutions. They demanded proportional representation and reservation of seats for Dalits in legislative bodies and decision-making positions.
     

 Additional Information

  • The Dalit Panthers movement drew inspiration from the Black Panthers in the United States, who fought against racial discrimination and police brutality. The term "Dalit" itself, meaning "oppressed" or "broken," was popularized by the Dalit Panthers to replace the derogatory term "untouchable" and assert a politicized identity.
  • The movement's founders, including Namdeo Dhasal and J.V. Pawar, were influential poets and writers who used their literary works to articulate the experiences and struggles of the Dalit community. The Dalit Panthers' literature, known as "Dalit Literature," became a significant cultural force, challenging dominant caste narratives and giving voice to the marginalized.
  • While the Dalit Panthers movement started in Maharashtra, it quickly spread to other parts of India, inspiring similar Dalit assertions and movements across the country. The movement faced challenges, including internal factionalism and ideological differences, which led to its eventual fragmentation.
  • Despite its decline, the Dalit Panthers movement had a lasting impact on Dalit consciousness and the broader struggle for social justice in India. It paved the way for the emergence of Dalit political parties, such as the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), and increased awareness about the need for Dalit empowerment and representation in various spheres of society.
  • The legacy of the Dalit Panthers continues to inspire Dalit activists and movements today, as the fight against caste-based discrimination and the assertion of Dalit identity remain crucial issues in contemporary Indian society.

questions.question: Which of the following is applied as a measure by the governments to neutralize the negative impact of fiscal drag?

options.text: Usually, personal tax allowances are increased.
options.html: Usually, personal tax allowances are increased.

questions.solution:
Personal Tax allowances are increased.

Key Points

  •  ‘Fiscal drag’ results in higher tax collections by the government but there is a fall in total demand in the economy (the negative impact of ‘fiscal
    drag’ or this is what we call as ‘fiscal drag’).
  • The best way is to provide some cushion on the front of personal tax (direct taxes which are paid by individuals such as income tax, interest tax, dividend tax,
    etc.)

Additional Information

  •  Fiscal drag’ is the restraining effect of the progressive taxation economies feel on their expansion. As people move from lower to higher tax brackets (slabs), the demand created by them falls (as they pay more personal tax).

questions.question: Which of the following is a special power of the Lok Sabha? Impeachment of the President of India. No-confidence motion passed against the Council of Ministers. ratifying the proclamation of emergency Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following is a special power of the Lok Sabha?
  1. Impeachment of the President of India.
  2. No-confidence motion passed against the Council of Ministers.
  3. ratifying the proclamation of emergency
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
No-confidence motion passed against the Council of Ministers is the correct answer.

Key Points
  • The President may declare an emergency under Article 352 of the Constitution when a state of war, external attack, or armed insurrection has developed or is imminent.
  • Within one month of the proclamation's issuance, a special majority of each House of Parliament (a majority of the entire membership of the House and a minimum (two-thirds majority) of the members present and voting) must approve it.
  • As a result, the Lok Sabha does not have sole authority to issue an emergency declaration regarding the confirmation of the Proclamation.
  • The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, according to Article 75 (3) of the Constitution.
  • No-confidence motions can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
  • This indicates that the Council of Ministers will only remain as long as the lower house believes in it.
  • That is, by passing a no-confidence resolution, the Lok Sabha can depose the Council of Ministers.
  • Article 61 of the Constitution specifies the mechanism for impeaching the President.
  • In terms of impeaching the President, both Houses of Parliament have equal authority.

Additional Information

  • The impeachment accusations are signed by one-fourth of the Lok Sabha members. The President of India is issued a 14-day notice. The impeachment accusations are then passed by Lok Sabha with a two-thirds majority and sent to Rajya Sabha.
  • In India, a state of emergency is a period of rule that can be declared by the President of India in particular crisis situations. The President can overturn various articles of the Constitution, which guarantees Fundamental Rights to Indian citizens, with the advice of the cabinet of ministers.
  • Part XVIII of the Indian Constitution, from Article 352 to 360, contains emergency measures. These laws enable the Central Government to efficiently respond to any exceptional circumstance.
  • The rationale for incorporation is to protect the country's sovereignty, unity, integrity, and security, as well as the democratic political system and the Constitution.
  • The Constitution defines three kinds of emergencies:
  1. National emergency 
  2. Constitutional emergency 
  3. Financial emergency

Key Points

  • Rabindranath Tagore composed several patriotic songs during the 'Swadeshi' movement to inspire the masses against colonial rule.
  • He renounced his knighthood in 1919 as a protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, where British forces killed hundreds of innocent Indians.
  • Tagore did not refuse the Nobel Prize; he accepted it in 1913 for his literary masterpiece "Gitanjali."
  • Statements (i) and (ii) are correct, while statement (iii) is incorrect.
  • Rabindranath Tagore was the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, highlighting his global influence.

Additional Information

  • Jallianwala Bagh Massacre: Occurred on April 13, 1919, when British troops under General Dyer opened fire on a peaceful gathering, killing hundreds.
  • Swadeshi Movement: A nationalist movement launched in 1905 to promote indigenous goods and boycott British products.
  • Knighthood: Rabindranath Tagore was awarded the title of "Sir" by the British in 1915 but renounced it in 1919 after the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy.
  • Gitanjali: A collection of poems by Tagore, for which he received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, emphasizing themes of spirituality and humanism.
  • Legacy: Tagore's contributions to literature, music, and art continue to inspire generations worldwide, and he remains a symbol of resistance against oppression.

questions.question: In 1916, Muslim League and Indian National Congress came to an understanding with each other and signed which among the following?
questions.questionHtml: In 1916, Muslim League and Indian National Congress came to an understanding with each other and signed which among the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lucknow Pact.

Key Points

  • The Lucknow Pact was signed in 1916 between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League.
  • This agreement marked a significant step in the unity of Hindus and Muslims in the fight against British colonial rule.
  • The pact was the outcome of mutual cooperation and was adopted during the Lucknow session of the Congress, presided over by Ambica Charan Mazumdar.
  • It laid down a framework for joint demands for greater autonomy and self-rule in India, including provisions for separate electorates for Muslims.
  • Key leaders involved in the pact included Bal Gangadhar Tilak from Congress and Muhammad Ali Jinnah from the Muslim League.

Additional Information

  • Indian National Congress:
    • Founded in 1885, the Congress was a major political party advocating for Indian self-rule.
    • By 1916, it sought alliances with other groups to strengthen the nationalist movement.
  • All India Muslim League:
    • Founded in 1906, the League represented Muslim interests in Indian politics.
    • It played a key role in advocating for separate electorates through the Lucknow Pact.
  • Separate Electorates:
    • This system allowed specific religious groups, like Muslims, to vote for their own representatives.
    • The provision was aimed at ensuring minority representation in legislative bodies.
  • Impact of Lucknow Pact:
    • It strengthened Hindu-Muslim unity, which was instrumental in the subsequent nationalist movements.
    • The pact demonstrated that collective demands could challenge British colonial policies effectively.

questions.questionHtml: Which regional music is characterized by vigorous rhythm and often accompanied by dance in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lavani.

Key Points

  • Lavani is a traditional folk music genre of Maharashtra characterized by its vigorous rhythm and is often performed with accompanying dance.
  • The word "Lavani" is derived from the term "Lavanya," which means beauty. It is intended to entertain and mesmerize audiences with its melodious songs and vibrant dance.
  • This music form traditionally blends music, poetry, and dance and is performed on a dholki (a percussion instrument) to create energetic rhythms.
  • Lavani performances are known for their expressive storytelling, often featuring themes of love, social commentary, or satire.
  • Historically, Lavani became a popular form of entertainment during the Peshwa era in the 18th century, particularly to boost the morale of soldiers.

Additional Information

  • Baul:
    • Baul is a unique folk music tradition from Bengal (West Bengal and Bangladesh).
    • It is performed by mystic minstrels known as Bauls and emphasizes spirituality and the philosophy of universal love.
    • Baul music uses traditional instruments such as the ektara, dotara, and khamak.
  • Kajri:
    • Kajri is a folk music form from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, especially popular in the eastern regions.
    • It is associated with the monsoon season and is characterized by lyrics that express longing and love.
    • Kajri is particularly performed by women and is accompanied by traditional instruments like tabla and harmonium.
  • Powada:
    • Powada is another traditional folk form from Maharashtra.

    • It is often performed in theatrical settings like Tamasha, a form of Marathi theatre.
    • Lavani has both sensual and social commentary forms, with the former being more common in entertainment settings and the latter in addressing societal issues.

Important Points

  • Evolution of Lavani: Lavani evolved over centuries, gaining prominence during the Maratha Empire. It served as both a form of entertainment and a means to convey messages.

questions.question: The Patiala Gharana is notable for its rendering of which types of classical music? 1. Thumri II. Khyal
questions.questionHtml:
The Patiala Gharana is notable for its rendering of which types of classical music?
1. Thumri
II. Khyal
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

Key Points

  • The Patiala Gharana is one of the most prominent gharanas (schools of music) in Hindustani classical music, especially known for its rich and melodious style.
  • The gharana is particularly renowned for its unique and intricate rendering of the Khyal style of singing. Statement II is correct.
  • It is also famous for its emotive and expressive performances of Thumri, a lighter form of classical music that focuses on romantic and devotional themes. Statement I is correct.
  • Singers of the Patiala Gharana are known for their ability to use intricate ornamentation such as taans (rapid melodic passages) and bol-baant (division of lyrics in rhythmic patterns).
  • Since the gharana excels in both Khyal and Thumri, the correct answer is Both I and II.

Additional Information

  • Khyal:
    • Khyal is a major vocal genre in Hindustani classical music and is characterized by its improvisation and elaboration of ragas.
    • The word "Khyal" means "imagination," and it allows artists to showcase their creativity within the framework of a raga.
    • The Patiala Gharana has developed its own distinctive style of Khyal, characterized by elaborate and fast-paced taans.
  • Thumri:
    • Thumri is a semi-classical form of Indian music, often associated with romantic, devotional, or light-hearted themes.
    • It is typically rendered in ragas such as Khamaj, Pilu, and Desh, which allow for more emotional and flexible expressions.
    • The Patiala Gharana is celebrated for its soulful and emotive Thumri performances.
  • Features of the Patiala Gharana:
    • The gharana originated in the royal court of Patiala, Punjab, during the 19th century.
    • It emphasizes intricate and rapid taans, the use of bol-taans, and an overall melodious approach.
    • Famous exponents include Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, Ustad Amanat Ali Khan, and Ustad Fateh Ali Khan.
  • Other Prominent Gharanas:
    • Gwalior Gharana: Known for its foundational Khyal style.
    • Kirana Gharana: Focuses on slow and elaborate development of ragas.
    • Agra Gharana: Combines dhrupad and Khyal styles.
    • Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana: Known for its mastery over rare and complex ragas.

Important Points

  • Thumri and Khyal:
    • While Khyal is a more structured and classical form, Thumri allows for greater emotional expression and storytelling.
    • The Patiala Gharana has managed to excel in both, showcasing its versatility and depth in Hindustani classical music.
  • Importance of Gharanas:
    • Gharanas play a vital role in preserving and transmitting the rich traditions of Indian classical music.
    • Each gharana has its own unique style, repertoire, and techniques, contributing to the diversity of Indian classical music.

questions.question: What is the binary representation of decimal number 92? 1) 1100001 2) 1011100 3) 1011110 4) 1011001
questions.questionHtml:
What is the binary representation of decimal number 92?

1) 1100001

2) 1011100

3) 1011110

4) 1011001
questions.solution:
Option 4 is correct.

Concept:-

To convert decimal to binary number, a division method can be used. In this method divide the decimal number with 2 until the quotient remains zero, and note the remainders for each division of quotient.

Method:

  • Take the last remainder as Most significant bit (MSB) and the first remainder as Least significant bit (LSB).
  • Read the remainders from MSB to LSB. The resulting binary sequence will be the binary number for the given decimal number.

questions.question: Which type of Operating system is also known as a command-line interface?
questions.questionHtml: Which type of Operating system is also known as a command-line interface?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is a CUI-based operating system.

Key Points

  • Character User Interface-based operating system (CUI-based operating system):
    • ​This type of operating system requires a user to type the instructions for the computer in a specific format.
    • Then the operating system interprets the commands and generates the corresponding computer instructions.
    • Hence, the user needs to remember the commands to interact with the computer.
    • This type of operating system is also known as a command-line interface (CLI) and it displays data character by character and is only textual in nature.
    • MS-DOS and UNIX are examples of CUI-based operating systems.​

Additional Information

  • Graphical User Interface-based operating system (GUI-based operating system):
    • ​The GUI-based operating system uses graphics to make the program easy to use.
    • The GUI has menus, pointers, and icons on the screen. An icon is a picture, that represents applications, and a pointer is a symbol, which is displayed on the monitor.
    • A mouse is used to move the pointer to an icon and one of the mouse buttons is pressed to activate the application associated with that icon.
    • A GUI-based operating system is slower and takes more hard disk space.
    • MS Windows and Linux are examples of this type of operating system
  • Single-user operating system:
    • ​This type of operating system can process instructions from only one user at a time.
    • A personal computer is a popular single-user system.
    • UT is a general-purpose system that can execute programs to perform a wide variety of tasks.
    • MS-DOS (disk operating system), and Windows 95 are examples of a single-user operating systems.
  • Multi-user operating system:
    • ​Multiuser operating system allows more than one user to work simultaneously on an operating system.
    • It is also capable of running multiple programs concurrently and can share resources, such as printers and disks.
    • It can simultaneously process instruction from multiple users and users work on different computers but a single computer performs their individual tasks simultaneously but independently of each other.
    • Linux is an example of multi-user operating system.

questions.question: Which of the following in a computer, stores BIOS?

questions.solution:

Key Points

  • CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor) is a technology for constructing integrated circuits. It is also a term used to refer to the chip that stores the BIOS settings in a computer.
  • The BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) is firmware used to perform hardware initialization during the booting process and to provide runtime services for operating systems and programs.
  • While the BIOS itself is stored in ROM (Read-Only Memory), the settings and configurations that the BIOS uses are stored in the CMOS chip, which requires power to maintain the information.
  • In summary, the CMOS chip stores the BIOS settings, making it crucial for the proper booting and configuration of the computer system.

Additional Information

  • Option 2: CPU - This is incorrect because the CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the main processing unit of the computer and does not store the BIOS.
  • Option 3: HDD - This is incorrect because the HDD (Hard Disk Drive) is used for data storage and does not store the BIOS.
  • Option 4: RAM - This is incorrect because RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile memory used for temporary storage of data and does not store the BIOS.
